To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nuclear matrix element (NME) of the neutrino-less double beta decay (0νββ), is strongly quenched by differences in deformation (or quadrupole correlation) between the parent and grand daughter nucleus.

1) the deformation of the nuclei is crucial for the NME, and 2) the NME's calculated in the framework of QRPA are underestimated due to the spherical nature of this model, and 3) the effects of the SRC on the 0ν2β decay are small.

the nuclear matrix elements are strongly quenched by differences in the quadrupole correlations, and that the NMEs obtained in the framework on the Interacting Shell model and QRPA can be reconciled by the inclusion of the short range correlation effects in both approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of nuclear matrix elements of 0νβ decay in the Interacting Shell model and Quasiparticle Random Phase Approximation (QRPA).
the study of the nuclear structure of the nuclei involved in 0νβ decay, and the implications of the nuclear structure in the NME.

the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) of the neutrino-less double beta decay (ββ) in the framework of two different approaches, namely, the Interacting Shell model and the Quasi-particle Random-Phase Approximation (QRPA).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NME of the 76 Ge decay lies in the range 0.5-1.5.
the NME of 0νβ decay are still uncertain by a factor 3.

the QRPA and the Interacting Shell model NME's are in good agreement, but the NME's from the QRPA are systematically smaller, by 10-15% in the case of the QRPA with the renormalized 0νβ decay operator, and by 25-35% in the case with the original operator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NME for the 76Ge is in the range 0.2 - 0.4 and that the uncertainties are dominated by the lack of information about the wave functions of 76Ge and 76Se.
the NME for the neutrinoless beta beta decays is a model dependent quantity, which depends strongly on the nuclear model used to describe the nuclear wave function.
the nuclear matrix elements are strongly sensitive to the quadrupole correlations, and that the Interacting Shell model and the QRPA are able to describe them with comparable accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear matrix element for the 0ν2β decay is a very sensitive probe of nuclear structure.
the NME of the 0ν double beta decay is very sensitive to the quadrupole correlations of the nuclei involved in the decay.
the NME of the 76 Ge decay is about 50% larger than in the standard calculations.
